column2: Build a Library

Verena gave mankind the written word, and the Order of Mysteries keeps what was written. A brother of the Order without a library of his own is a scholar without a desk, and you must build one in which the lost lore you recover can be studied, copied and kept.
To complete this mission, take the decision §Y'Build a Library'§! in the Intrigue menu and see the building through to the end.
Find an Apprentice

Every Lorekeeper worth the name takes on an apprentice. Somebody must copy the crumbling scrolls, keep the catalogue in order and carry the lantern down into the ruins, and what [Root.GetTitle] has the time to do all that alone?
§Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! must name an apprentice through the §YMinor Titles§! screen, or keep [Root.GetHerHis] eyes open for a promising pupil, to complete this mission.
Recover a Lost Text

Your colleague [FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName] has come upon a letter naming the hiding places of several lost writings. A bargain has been struck: [FromFrom.GetFirstName] brings the letter and the learning, you pay for the expedition, and the Order of Mysteries shall have the find for its Mysterious Volumes.
If §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! sets out on one of the expeditions §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! suggests and finds the lost text, the mission is completed.
Raid the Hoard of [FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName]

[FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName] hoards books like a Scrollbearer, locking away what Verena gave to all. The Goddess teaches that knowledge belongs to everyone, and in that spirit you and a colleague have agreed to break into [FromFrom.GetFirstName]'s library, carry off what [FromFrom.GetSheHe] will not share and leave [FromFrom.GetHerHis] scriptorium in no state to hoard any more. Not a single page will burn, of course. You are not Witch Hunters.
Your colleague will bring you to the library of §Y[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]§!. If you take or wreck something and get away unseen, the mission is completed.
Tablet of Lybaras

A tablet of green stone from the sealed archives of Lybaras, the city of scholars of old Nehekhara, where the priest kings made inventors and stargazers of their subjects. Its glyphs record the laws by which one substance becomes another and the courses of the stars above the desert. Every scholar who has read a line of it calls it the greatest find of the Order of Mysteries, and every Witch Hunter calls it something else.
whether it's true that I keep a tablet from the tombs of Lybaras at home or not

A true library takes years and gold to assemble, and without one I shall never see further than the next village. The Lorekeepers say that Verena lifted mankind from barbarism with the gift of writing. It is time I gave those writings a proper home.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena10]
For knowledge!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena10]
On second thought, there are more pressing matters.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena10]

Where shall the library stand? What I mean to keep there will frighten the ignorant, tempt my brothers and sisters of the Order and, sooner or later, draw a Witch Hunter to my door. Many a Lorekeeper hides the books deep within the castle walls, but a hall open to every honest reader is what the Goddess truly asks of us.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena11]
Deep within the walls of [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName], where no zealot will find it.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena11]
The library must fit into your castle. Your books will be safe, but your household will live beside them.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_hidden_tt]
In a hall open to every scholar, as Verena wills.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena11]
Nothing will stand in the way of a fine library, but anyone may walk in.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_open_tt]
In a guarded house on an island, where only boats can reach it.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTCverena11]
In a guarded house far out in the country.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTDverena11]
Far from prying eyes the library can be as large as it needs to be, and a thief will have to find it first.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_remote_tt]

The master builder has unrolled his plans across my table. A reading room with a few shelves would serve. So would a scriptorium with copying desks, or a hall of learning with a reading gallery under a painted ceiling of owls. And then there is the drawing he keeps at the bottom of the pile, the one modelled on the Grand Temple of Verena at Nuln.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena12]
A reading room will do.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena12]
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a small but useful library.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_small_tt]
A scriptorium, with desks for copyists.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena12]
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a library where books can be copied as well as read.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_medium_tt]
A hall of learning, worthy of the Order.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTCverena12]
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a great library with reading rooms, a scriptorium and an archive.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_large_tt]
Something to make the Lorekeepers of Nuln weep with envy.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTDverena12]
[Root.GetFullName] will build a library to rival the Grand Temple of Nuln, with every gallery, vault and desk the plans can hold.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_grand_tt]

A library is only as good as its copyists. The scribes of the town write a fair hand for contracts and tavern signs, but the brothers of the Temple of Clio the Scrivener at Carroburg copy a crumbling scroll so faithfully that the copy outlives the original by a thousand years. They do not come cheap.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena13_scribes]
The town scribes will learn.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena13_scribes]
Send for the scriveners of Carroburg.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena13_scribes]

Every Verenan remembers the sack of Wolfenburg, when the Order wept more for the burning books than for the dead. Tallow candles are cheap, and so are buckets of sand. Stone vaults and shuttered lanterns of Nuln brass are not.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena13_lamps]
Candles and sand. We shall be careful.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena13_lamps]
No flame shall touch these shelves unshuttered.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena13_lamps]

Half the old books I mean to keep are falling apart in my hands. The local tanner offers calfskin for new bindings, while the binders of Marienburg work in vellum and boards that keep out damp, worm and the careless thumb alike, for a merchant's price.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena13_bindings]
The tanner's calfskin will hold.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena13_bindings]
Only Marienburg bindings for my books.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena13_bindings]

And then the books themselves, the heart of every library and, to the Cult of Verena, holy every one of them. I have a fair number already. A fair number is not a library. The booksellers of Altdorf have lists, the University of Nuln sells its spare copies, and the printers have begun to flood the Empire with cheap books, to the horror of the followers of Scripsisti.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena13_books]
The books I have will be quite enough for now.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena13_books]
Buy every book worth the reading!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena13_books]
[Root.GetFullName] will spare [Root.GetHerHis] purse, and the library will be the poorer for it.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_cheap_tt]
[Root.GetFullName] will pay for the best, and the library will be the better for it.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_fine_tt]

It is hardly the Grand Temple of Nuln, and a visiting Lorekeeper would call it a cupboard with ambitions, but it is mine. The shelves stand, the desk is lit and the catalogue fits on a single page. The Owl will show me the way from here.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena15_simple]

The work is done. My library may not compare to the great libraries of Altdorf and Nuln, but its shelves are full, its copyists busy and its catalogue in good order. It will serve me well in the search for what the world has forgotten.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena15_normal]

The library is finished, and it is a fine one. Scholars write to ask whether they may read in it, and a passing Knight of the Scroll stood in the doorway for some time before he remembered to take off his helmet. Will it bring me the wisdom I seek? Only Verena knows.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena15_good]
Time to open the books...
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena15_simple]
Let the reading begin!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena15]
The Ambition of a [Root.GetTitle]
[Root.LabText_EVTNAMEverena16_great]
The House of Learning
[Root.LabText_EVTNAMEverena16_best]

After months of hard work and a small fortune in gold, the library of [Root.GetFullName] is the envy of every Lorekeeper who hears of it. Its galleries hold the learning of half the Old World, its scriptorium copies a dozen books a season and its archive keeps writings that even the Order of Mysteries thought lost. It stands as a monument to the [Root.GetTitle]'s ambition.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena16_great]

No expense was spared. Under the eye of [Root.GetFullName] a house of learning has risen that is spoken of in Altdorf, Marienburg and Nuln alike. The owls carved over the gate keep watch over vaults of stone, a scriptorium of forty desks and a reading hall where the [Root.GetTitle]'s own scales of Verena hang above the catalogue.\n\nHigh Priestess van der Perssen herself has written to ask when she may come to debate on its steps. It wants only its master to begin.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena16_best]
Follow the Owl!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena16_great]
Let the debating begin!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena16_best]

The whole castle woke to shouting in the night. A lamp left burning in the reading room has fallen into a heap of loose pages, and by the time the bucket chain reached it the new shelves were ablaze. We saved most of the books, Verena be praised, but not everyone came out unhurt.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena17]
Better skin than books, alas.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena17]
We must guard against fire properly this time...
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena17]
[Root.GetFullName] will spend gold on stone vaults and shuttered lanterns, so the library suffers less.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_fire_tt]

A preacher of Sigmar has been haranguing the market square for three days. 'Heretics! Every temple of Verena harbours forbidden writings, and now the [Root.GetTitle] is building another nest for them!' This morning a small mob gathered at the gate demanding to know which books I keep, and whether any of them have been written by daemons.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena18]
Show them the shelves. Let them see there is nothing to fear.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena18]
[Root.GetFullName] will change [Root.GetHerHis] plans to calm the townsfolk rather than to build the best library.
[Root.LabText_verena_library_rabble_tt]
Since when does the [Root.GetTitle] answer to a rabble?
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena18]

Disaster! A sweet, rotten smell from the cellar led my servants to the crates of books I bought this spring. Damp has crept into the bindings, black mould blooms across the pages and the bookworms have eaten their way through a whole treatise on canon law. So much for leaving them there until the shelves were ready.
[Root.LabText_EVTDESCverena19]
Save what can be saved.
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTAverena19]
Build a dry store for them, at once!
[Root.LabText_EVTOPTBverena19]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

It has come to my attention that you still have no library worth the name! I cannot imagine how you hope to recover the lost lore of Verena without proper shelves, copyists and an archive. My own library has become a second home to me, and to half the scholars of the province. You would do well to follow my example, or your work will be forgotten before the ink is dry.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

Master, forgive my boldness, but I fear we are both held back for want of a proper library. Every book we recover ends up in a chest under my bed, and the mice have already eaten a chapter of the Mysterious Volumes. If we are to keep what Verena gave us, we need shelves, desks and a dry vault. Build a library, Master, I beg you.

Your devoted apprentice,
[From.GetFirstName]

With a library of my own I can take on mysteries I would not have dared before. How I ever worked from a chest of books and a kitchen table I shall never understand. The lost lore of Verena is within my reach.

My new library is the envy of my brothers and sisters of the Order. Even Manfred Archibald, who founded the Order of Mysteries and has seen the archives of every great temple in the Empire, would be hard pressed to find fault with it.
My work has only begun.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

I must say, dear colleague, I do not know how you manage without an apprentice! Mine copies a page faster than any scrivener of Clio, carries the lantern into the foulest crypt without a word of complaint and has never once smelled of ale. Take my advice and find one of your own.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

For months the thought of an apprentice has followed me about the castle. None of my councillors would do, and I dare not ask the priests of the town. But one of my servants has caught my eye. [From.GetFirstName] reads every scrap of paper [From.GetSheHe] dusts, and this morning I found [From.GetHerHim] correcting the Classical in one of my own notes.
[From.GetSheHeCap] knows how to listen, at the very least.
Surely I can find someone worthier than a servant!
You keep looking for an apprentice.

I have a good feeling about this! With [From.GetFirstName] as my apprentice there is no end to what we may recover. Lost tombs, forgotten archives, perhaps even a page or two that never made it into the Mysterious Volumes.
Bright times are ahead.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My [Root.GetSisterBrother], I have a proposal that may interest you. Not long ago an old letter came into my hands, written by a brother of the Order of Mysteries who died before he could follow it up. It names the hiding places of several lost writings. You have the purse and I have the letter. Shall we search for them together, in the true spirit of the Order?

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

The letter names three lost texts. A tome among the stock of an antiquarian in [Root.Capital.GetName], a scroll walled up in a temple at [temple_site.GetName], and a tablet in the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName] in [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. The further we go, the older the find and the greater its secrets. The choice is yours.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

I bring the best of news! Since I last wrote, I have bought from a Tilean tomb robber a map that leads to a sealed archive of Lybaras, the city of scholars of old Nehekhara, where the priest kings kept their inventors and stargazers. If the map is true, the archive holds the Tablet of Lybaras itself. I will not hide the danger. Brother Oliver's expedition into the Land of the Dead went looking for the Book of Dust, and he alone came back. The other places remain, the tome in [Root.Capital.GetName], the scroll in [temple_site.GetName] and the tablet in [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName], but I would argue that a chance like this comes once in a lifetime.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
To Lybaras, and may the dead stay asleep.
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out across the Great Desert for the sealed archive of Lybaras. This chance will not come again in your lifetime.\n
Let us travel to the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName].
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out for [ruin_site.GetName], hoping to find the tablet in the ruins there.\n
a successful search.\n
The scroll in [temple_site.GetName] seems the wisest choice.
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out for [temple_site.GetName], hoping to find the scroll in a temple there.\n
I have little to spare... Surely the antiquarian will do?
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! go through the stock of an antiquarian in search of the old tome.\n
The Tablet of Lybaras

When we found the door to the archive, carved with the scales and stars of Lybaras, we could hardly believe our eyes. [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I had nearly given up. We had seen the bone-white sentinels pacing the dunes at dusk and heard something vast moving beneath the sand, and that day was to be the last of our search. Surely only the Goddess could have led us there! My hands shook as I helped the servants heave the last stone aside.\n\nLantern held high, my colleague and I went in first. The light fell on jars of sealed scrolls, star charts painted across the walls and the bronze gears of some engine of the old priest kings. And something deep within the chamber gave the light back, something vividly green... [From.GetFirstName]'s breath came quick and shallow. 'It... it cannot be!'
The learning of Lybaras returns to the world. Praise Verena!

Our journey into foreign lands met with no small amount of trouble, but at last we reached the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName] safely. After a fortnight of digging the servants laid bare the mouth of a buried chamber. [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went in side by side, and the lantern showed us a tablet set into the far wall, its glyphs untouched by a thousand years.
Are those glyphs Nehekharan, or older still?

A generous gift to the temple of [temple_site.GetName] persuaded its priest to open the inner chambers to us. We searched every niche and crypt for the hiding place of the scroll, and on the fifth day a servant called us to a loose stone behind the altar...
We found it, [From.GetFirstName]!

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went through every shelf and chest of the dusty little shop. For days on end we did nothing but breathe dust and leaf through almanacs, sermons and bad poetry. So you may imagine my surprise when, on the fourth day, an owl looked up at me from the spine of a battered old book.
I think this is it, [From.GetFirstName]!

My doubts began soon after we left the last oasis, but [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] swore we had only misread the map. After every empty valley [From.GetSheHe] had a new idea, and after every night we lost more servants to the things that walk the dunes. When at last we fled north with half the camels and none of the gold, a suspicion crept over me... What if the map was forged, and [From.GetFirstName] knew it all along? Was the whole expedition a plot to ruin me?

Our journey into foreign lands met with every trouble the road can offer, from foul weather to lame horses, but our guide was the end of it. When that scoundrel ran off with the last of our gold, we found that we were not even in the right part of [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName]!

A generous gift to the temple of [temple_site.GetName] persuaded its priest to open the inner chambers to us. We searched every niche and crypt for the hiding place of the scroll, and after a week we had found nothing more interesting than a bundle of rather lewd letters. We had to admit defeat.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went through every shelf and chest of the dusty little shop. For days on end we did nothing but breathe dust and leaf through almanacs, sermons and bad poetry. After a week we had to admit defeat. There was nothing of worth in that place.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] is a pompous, featherbrained Scrollbearer. You know it to be true, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]! [infiltration_target.GetSheHeCap] buys up every book in the province and lets no one read them, not even the Order. It is time someone set them free. Let us break into [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library, carry off what [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] hoards and leave [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] scriptorium in no state to hoard any more!

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My friend, we have a common foe. You know of whom I speak, that miser [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName]! A member of our Order who locks away the gifts of Verena like a dragon on its gold. It makes me sick! Let us break into [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library and share with the world what [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] will not.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] sits on the finest hoard of books and curiosities in the province and has not lent out so much as an almanac in ten years. The Scrollbearers would be proud. What do you say, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]? Shall we pay [infiltration_target.GetHerHim] a visit by night and claim what should belong to all?

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Most esteemed [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My spies have not yet found where [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] keeps [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library. Do not worry, my friend, they have several promising leads. A cart of books bought in Altdorf must go somewhere. We need only be patient.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
I shall be ready to leave at a moment's notice.
As soon as the spies of §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! have found the library, you will set out.\n

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] must be as fearful as [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] is greedy, for [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library is a walled house far from any road. As we creep closer under cover of night, [From.GetFirstName] whispers to me about the guards. A Knight of the Scroll, by the look of the armour, and two hired swords. We will only get one chance at this.

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] has hidden [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library deep beneath [infiltration_target.Capital.GetName]. Thanks to [From.GetFirstName]'s spies we have come this far unseen, but the last door is guarded, and the guards look awake.

'It was not hard to find [infiltration_target.GetFirstName]'s library,' [From.GetFirstName] tells me as we slip into the [infiltration_target.Capital.GetHolding]. 'Old [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] cannot keep a secret to save [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] life, but [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] does know how to hire good guards.' [From.GetSheHeCap] points down the corridor, at the problem ahead.
I have a way with people, and a heavy purse.
You try to bribe the guards.\n
I brewed a sleeping draught for this very moment.
You try to drug the guards with a draught of your own making.\n
a successful scheme.
a failed scheme, and discovery.
You draw them off, I will slip inside.
§Y[infiltration_companion.GetTitledFirstName]§! tries to lure the guards away. You will have to do the work inside alone, so you can do less harm.\n
On second thought, this is madness...
You slip away and go home to your [Root.Capital.GetHolding].\n

As we step out of the shadows the guards draw their swords, but their faces change when I lift the heavy purse from my belt. After a few quiet words and the clink of coin, [infiltration_companion.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] and I pass through the heavy door into a hall of shelves that reaches up into darkness. 'Well, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]?' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] whispers. 'How shall we go about it?'

By some miracle, [infiltration_companion.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] manages to empty the little vial into the jug before it is carried to the guards. Within a quarter of an hour they are snoring softly. 'We must hurry, the draught will not last forever,' I whisper as we step over them. Inside, the shelves reach up into darkness. 'Well?' [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] asks. 'How shall we go about it?'
You wreck the scriptorium, I will find the books.
You split up to cover more ground. Quicker, but riskier.\n
Leave the scriptorium to me. Take whatever you can carry.
Help me find where [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] keeps [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] best books.
You stay together. Safer, but you can do less.\n
Let us leave this place in no state to hoard ever again!

Everything went so well at first. [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] emptied the vial into the jug without anyone noticing. That was half an hour ago. The guards show no sign of drowsiness, one of them is singing, and our time is running out. I whisper my apologies as we creep away, but [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] does not answer.
That recipe has never failed me before, I swear...

I had my doubts, but I must admit I am impressed! [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] drew the guards off by crying fire in the stable yard, and they ran out with their buckets as one man. Every Verenan knows that cry would clear any library in the Empire. I do not know how long I have. What now?
Find the rarest books and the hidden cabinet!
Wreck the scriptorium, scatter the catalogue!

I have seen many foolish things in my day, but [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName]'s distraction may take the prize. [infiltration_companion.GetSheHeCap] began to rattle a chain against the wall and wail like a ghost of the library! When the guards' footsteps came closer I seized [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the sleeve and ran. 'A ghost? Really? Nobody with any sense would fall for that!'
There will be no second attempt tonight. Nor for a long, long time.

I am about to sweep the copying desks clear when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and find myself face to face with the guards. Our eyes meet for a moment before I drop the inkpot and run, but it is no use. Even half-drugged they are faster than me.

I am about to sweep the copying desks clear when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and look straight into the panicked eyes of [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName], and only then do I see the guards holding [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the arms. 'Run!' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] cries, but it is too late.

My arms are full of books from the hidden cabinet when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and find myself face to face with the guards. Our eyes meet for a moment before I drop the books and run, but it is no use. Even half-drugged they are faster than me.

My arms are full of books from the hidden cabinet when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and look straight into the panicked eyes of [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName], and only then do I see the guards holding [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the arms. 'Run!' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] cries, but it is too late.
Unhand me! I am a colleague of your [infiltration_target.GetMasterMistress]!

It seems my guards have caught a pair of rats among the shelves! [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and [From.GetHerHis] accomplice [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] tried to break into my library and help themselves to my books. Brothers of the Order, if you please! Such an insult cannot go unanswered...
Perhaps [From.GetFirstName] will trade a few secrets for [From.GetHerHis] freedom.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! refuses to share [From.GetHerHis] secrets and stays in the cell.\n
Leave them in the dungeon. I will deal with them later...

I had come to the point of begging for water when the guards dragged me out of the cell. I must have fainted, for the next thing I see is the scornful face of [From.GetFirstName]. 'Well, well. A thief who calls [Root.GetHerselfHimself] a brother of the Order! Verena is the goddess of justice too, you know.' After a few more insults, [From.GetSheHe] offers me my freedom in exchange for the secrets of my own library.
Give me water, and I will tell you whatever you wish.
You will never be worthy of my secrets!
You stay in the cell.\n

If I ever find the thief who broke into my library, I will see [From.GetHerHim] hanged! It seems I have made an enemy, for the intruder came to wreck, not to steal. I concentrate for a long time and almost begin to doubt myself, but then I see it: faint ripples, one shadow, then two. A fire, and a sword above it, and the sword is red.
I see a still pond under the twin moons. Two swans glide across it side by side, and then one of them is gone, and the other is alone on the water.

I am not sure at first what to make of the shape. A shadow, a trick of the candle? But it is there, plain as day: a familiar figure standing beneath Mannslieb, with Morrslieb rising green behind.
I see a pair of scales, the scales of Verena, hanging in the dark. Slowly, one pan sinks while the other rises, and on the rising pan lies a crown.
At first there are only lines in the water. Or are they? Yes, a forest, a vast forest, and an owl circling above it in the moonlight before it settles on a single tower.

Into the woods, with basket and sickle.
On the hunt. Some ingredients have to be taken fresh.
To the apothecaries of the town.

We came home with full baskets and green fingers. Faxtoryll by the stream, valerian at the edge of the clearing, and a patch of wormwood that no herbalist of the town has found before us. The cabinet smells of the forest for days.
The woods were not generous. Half the herbs I knew were trampled by boar or picked bare by the village wise woman before us, but I found a little, and a little is better than nothing.
I came home with an empty basket, wet boots and a stomach ache. I am fairly certain the mushroom I tasted in the clearing was not the one in the Principia Herbologium.

The hunt went well. A stag, a boar and a brace of hares, and I took from each what the old rites need: the heart, the liver, the eyes. The huntsmen stare at me as I work with my little knife, but they have learned not to ask.
We spent days in the forest and saw little game. In the end I took what I could from a single beast, and the huntsmen grumbled that a priest of Verena has no business on a hunt.
Nothing. Not a stag, not a boar, not so much as a hare. The huntsmen are already telling the story at court of the priest who scared off the game with his reading aloud.

The apothecaries knew what I wanted, or knew someone who did. Brimstone from the south, silver filings, a stoppered flask of aqua fortis, and a few things I paid for in the back room and did not ask about. A good haul, and an expensive one.
Half the stalls sold me coloured water and powdered chalk at the price of quicksilver. I bought what I could trust, which was not much.
Every apothecary in the town swore by his wares, and every one of them was a liar. I paid for the lesson and came home with nothing worth keeping.
A full cabinet, praise the Goddess.
Something at least.
A wasted journey.

The Order of Mysteries teaches that there are three roads to the hidden truth. The Lorekeepers read it in the stars, where the twenty signs of the Old World turn above the moons. The learned alchemists of Nuln and Altdorf seek it at the alembic, in what the world is made of. The stars.
The alembic.
The Goddess.

For years I have worked at the alembic, and it has shown me much. But there are other roads to the truth, and lately my mind wanders from the furnace.

I shall serve the Goddess.
No, I keep to my road.

The observatory.
The star charts of the old masters.

The twenty signs are as familiar to me now as the faces of my own family. Mammit the Wise and Mummit the Fool, the Big Cross, the Witchling Star, the Gloaming: I know where each one rises, and what it means for those born beneath it.
Verena gave us the stars to read.

The alchemists of Nuln say that everything in the world is made of a few simple things, and that the wise can take them apart and put them together again. At the furnace.
From the treatises.
My eyebrows have not grown back, and the stains on my fingers will never come off, but I know the secrets of the alembic now. What the world is made of holds few mysteries for me.
Knowledge is worth a pair of eyebrows.

The priests of Verena have always followed one of two schools. The Lorekeepers hold that learning is more important than justice, and spend their lives keeping what was written. The Lorekeepers. Learning comes first.
The Scalebearers. Justice comes first.
I have prayed and studied for months, and at last I feel the Goddess close: blind to all but the truth, holding Her scales and Her sword, with the owl on Her shoulder.
Go with the Owl.

Curse the weather.

The whole court stood on the walls in their furs, and the servants had brought hot wine. Just before midnight someone laughed, and then the star fell: a white streak from the Big Cross, exactly where I said it would be. The cheer could be heard in the town.

I sat alone on the roof with my charts and a lantern. Just before midnight the star fell: a white streak from the Big Cross, exactly where I said it would be. Nobody else saw it, but I know, and the Order will read it in the journal.
The whole court stood on the walls in their furs until well after midnight. Nothing fell. When the servants started to snigger, the guests went back inside one by one, and none of them looked at me.
I sat alone on the roof with my charts and a lantern until dawn. Nothing fell. At least nobody saw me waiting.
Verena has guided my hand on the charts.

Along with the rest of the inheritance, a cabinet of jars, pouches and stoppered flasks has come to me. Herbs, beast parts, salts: the cabinet of an alchemist. The Order could use these, or I could keep them for my own rites.

Along with the rest of the inheritance, a cabinet of jars, pouches and stoppered flasks has come to me. Herbs, beast parts, salts: the stuff of alchemists and wise women. My own brothers and sisters have little use for it.

Along with the rest of the inheritance, a cabinet of jars, pouches and stoppered flasks has come to me. Herbs, beast parts, salts: the stuff of alchemists and wise women. Whoever heard of a lord with a cabinet like this? The Witch Hunters may well ask.

Along with the rest of the inheritance, a big cabinet full of jars and pouches has come to me. Some of them smell funny, and one has eyes in it. My tutor says they are for alchemy and that I should not touch them.

Superstition. The Goddess is my ward.

It has been years since the scholars of the Order of Mysteries sat at one table. A symposium: a gathering of learned minds, each with their own studies, to make one great work that none could make alone. Your laboratory is fit for it, and Verena teaches that wisdom shared is wisdom doubled. But scholars are a jealous and quarrelsome lot, and the Order still whispers about the last symposium that ended with ink thrown in a rival's face.
Send out the invitations.
Call a §Ysymposium§! in your laboratory.

Then to work.

The disputation goes on until the candles gutter, and at the end of it the others are nodding at [FromFrom.GetFirstName], not at you. You have lost, in your own laboratory, and Verena does not favour those who cannot bear the truth.
We do it their way.
The guest's work is made.

Test the new theory.

Send [arguer_1.GetFirstName] home.

Send [arguer_2.GetFirstName] home.
Sending a guest home is a §Rscandal§!.
You weigh both complaints as Verena weighs a case, fairly and in the open, and in the end they shake hands. They will not be friends. But they will work.
Back to the work.

You step between them, and [arguer_1.GetFirstName] throws the ink anyway. It lands on you, and on three pages of the work, and everyone saw it.
This symposium is going badly.

You and [From.GetFirstName] fall into the work together without a word, one finishing the line of reasoning the other began, the way scholars do who have shared a study for years. You never had before.
Another cup, when we are done.

Late in the night, alone in your laboratory with the work in front of you, you hear an owl on the sill. You look up, and you see it. All of it, the whole shape of the work, every figure in its place. Your hands are shaking.
Wake the others. Now.
Your insight will make the work greater.

It is finished: a handgun, worked out from stolen Nuln designs and improved past anything the Gunnery School has made, rifled and true. When you fire it in the courtyard, the whole household runs to see.

It is finished: a compass of engraved brass whose needle always finds the north, even under the Chaos-tossed skies of the Sea of Claws. The merchant captains come to see it, and leave talking about nothing else.

It is finished: a radius astronomicus, a staff of brass and ebony that measures the angles of the stars, Mannslieb and the Witchling Star more precisely than any instrument in the Order's halls. Scholars will travel to see it.
It is finished: plans for a great crossbow on a turning carriage, and a first one built on your walls. The Imperial Engineers will grumble that scholars are doing their work.

It is finished: a furnace for your smelters, its draught and its bellows reckoned by the symposium, that burns hotter than any in the realm. The smiths will have more iron than they know what to do with.

It is finished: a cipher disc of two turning rings, and a way of writing that only a member of the Order can read. Secrets, debts, the names of cultists: none of it will be read by the wrong eyes again.
It is finished: a suit of plate armour, its joints reckoned by geometry so that it moves as freely as a coat. It is not the greatest work ever made at a symposium, but it is very good.
It is finished: a windmill with sails set by the symposium's figures, that grinds twice the grain. A useful thing, if not a glorious one.
It is finished: a pair of ground lenses in a wire frame that let an old scholar read the smallest hand as clearly as in youth. The elder members of the Order are very pleased.
Let the enemy hear it.
The captains will be grateful.
The stars are ours to read.
Let the greenskins come.
The smiths will be glad.
Let our enemies try to read it.
Good, honest work.
Bread is bread.
My old eyes thank you.

The work does not hold. The figures will not come right, however many times you reckon them, and in the end the scholars set down their pens and admit it. All that labour, and nothing to show for it but a stack of blotted pages.

The new theory is tested, and it is wrong. There is a flash, and a noise like the sky splitting, and then smoke and screaming. When it clears, the laboratory is a ruin of glass and fire, and not everyone at the symposium is still standing.
Verena teaches that failure is also knowledge.

Tell me how substances are weighed and changed.
Tell me what is written in the stars.
Tell me of the ways of the gods.

In my trance the presence spoke, and I understood. Truths hidden from mortals: of substances and the stars, of the will of the gods, of the lies men tell and the things not yet come to pass. When my soul returned to my body, I saw the world with new eyes. Verena has heard me.

The presence gave me an answer, and for many days since the rite I have tried to make sense of it. However long I study it, I cannot. Whatever I was meant to know is beyond me. I can only conclude that I am not worthy of the Goddess's wisdom.

The presence answered my question about hidden truths, and the answer was a riddle that changed each time I wrote it down. The more I study my notes, the less they say the same thing twice. I have begun to wonder whose voice it was in that room. Verena does not lie. Something else does.

The presence gave me a cryptic answer, but I have spent many nights over my notes since, and I believe I have worked out what it meant. Whether it was the Goddess's wisdom or my own wishful reading, time will tell.

Alone at my desk, quill in hand and a good supply of ink at my elbow, I stare down at the blank page. The size of the task dawns on me. I must set down all I know, and hide it from those who are unworthy of it.
It will take a great deal of time and effort, but it will be glorious!

I will write on the divine.
Rites to call on the gods and the contemplation that draws a mind near to theirs.
I will write on the stars.
The signs, the moons and the wandering stars, and what the heavens tell those who can read them.
I will write on the alembic.
Transmutation and the healing arts, by which flesh and metal alike may be perfected.
I have made good headway in setting down what I know of the divine, but it is still too much for one book. I must narrow the work further, to one of its two faces.

Contemplation brings a mind closer to the gods, and perhaps to true understanding.

The star signs.
The twenty signs hold a great store of knowledge, and the one who reads them well reads the fates of men.
The moons and the wandering stars.
Mannslieb, Morrslieb and the stars that wander reveal both the will of the gods and the natures of men.

A panacea would cure every sickness and hold back age, bringing the body to perfection.
Transmutation.
To turn base metal to gold is the first step to remaking oneself.

You may use them later tonight.

I arrived at the study with [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] closely behind me. 'This is the equipment I have obtained', I explained and gestured towards the neatly ordered collection of tools. [stargazing_guest.GetFirstName] inspected the collection for a moment, but did not look very impressed. Or at least, as if it were something [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] has seen before.
At least I like them.

Upon my arrival in [stargazing_host.Capital.GetName], I was received with great splendor. [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] explained that [stargazing_host.GetSheHe] had chosen a perfect location to use during the night. 'This way and I will show it to you.' [stargazing_host.GetSheHeCap] led the way to a hill not too far away. The hill had a decent height for its small size and no trees obscuring the view.
This will suit our needs perfectly!
A lonely hill in the middle of nowhere...

We walked to the hill of my choice not far away. Once there, [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] took a moment to look at the hill and the sky above. 'This hill should suit our needs perfectly I think.' [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] said while nodding approvingly. We quickly decided on where to set up in order to be able to see as much as possible.
It is all about location, location, location.

I walked with [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] to the nearby hill I had chosen for us. While pointing to a few places that I think would work well for us, I heard [stargazing_guest.GetFirstName] complaining behind me, clearly disapproving of my choice. 'I suppose it will do. But it seems to be very far away if you ask me.'
Trust me. It offers a better view.

When I arrived in [stargazing_host.Capital.GetName] I was not only met with a warm smile from [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName], but a grand feast as well! A wide range of courses had been prepared for our pleasure and indulgence. [stargazing_host.GetFirstName] raised a cup in my honor. 'Let us toast for a night of new discoveries!'
A spectacular feast I must say!
Is it not a bit excessive?

When [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] entered the dining hall, I think the feast came as a surprise. And a very pleasant one at that. We dined and enjoyed ourselves and had a good time just speaking with each other for the next few hours. 'You have outdone yourself, [stargazing_host.GetFirstName]. This was spectacular!'
The wonders of good food.

I showed [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] to the dining hall and the awaiting feast. The look on [stargazing_guest.GetHerHis] face made it abundantly clear that [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] was not expecting a proper feast. Perhaps [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] was expecting a small dinner? Did I overdo it?
It tasted good at least.

[stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] was there to welcome me on my arrival in [stargazing_host.Capital.GetName]. Shortly thereafter we made the way to [stargazing_host.GetFirstName]'s private study, where [stargazing_host.GetSheHe] began to show me [stargazing_host.GetHerHis] current work and most recent discoveries. 'How better to pass the time before nightfall than to spend it on studies and learning?'
That is why I am here.
Even learning is best in moderation.

Knowing that [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] is a learned scholar, I showed [stargazing_guest.GetHerHim] to my study. After discussing my most recently acquired writings I suggested that we sit down and try to learn something from them. [stargazing_guest.GetSheHeCap] responded with approval. 'I would never say no to an opportunity of gathering newfound knowledge. That is after all, the reason I am here.'
Knowledge is power.

Thinking that [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] would jump at the chance of examining my most recently acquired writings, I showed [stargazing_guest.GetHerHim] my collection. After a moment of glancing through the pages, [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] casually put the writings back in their place. [stargazing_guest.GetSheHeCap] then suggested that we rest before the night.
I presume the journey was long?

Night is almost upon us and the first stars are finally making themselves visible in the sky outside. I should tell [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] that it is time. Time to see if we can uncover new secrets.
We should get ready.

[stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] and I have been looking at the stars for a few hours already. Suddenly, it occurred to me. Stars are aligned in different patterns, taking on the shapes of different figures. But they are not really moving, are they? They always seem to have the same location in relation to one another.
[stargazing_guest.GetFirstName]! Take notes!

I was reading through our notes when [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] suddenly shouted at me. '[stargazing_guest.GetFirstName]! It just occurred to me!' [stargazing_host.GetSheHeCap] then went on explaining [stargazing_host.GetHerHis] theory about how the stars never move and how they are related to one another.
[stargazing_host.GetSheHeCap] could be on to something!

I was writing down some notes when I heard [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] speak behind me and turned to face [stargazing_guest.GetHerHim]. [stargazing_guest.GetSheHeCap] then went on to explain a theory of how the star signs are connected with each other and how they are aligned in a certain way.
Yes. Interesting thoughts.

When looking at the stars and the patterns they make in the sky, I started thinking about the star signs. I quickly explained my newfound theory to [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] who nodded in agreement. The star signs are sure to be hiding secrets waiting to be unveiled.
I am certain of it!

After several hours of studying the stars, I saw it. A sphere moving slowly across the sky with a long tail behind it. I called for [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] to get [stargazing_guest.GetHerHis] attention. We both marveled at the beauty of it for a while. 'There is something divine about it.' [stargazing_guest.GetFirstName] said after a moment of silence. I could only nod my head in agreement.
It makes us seem so small.

After several hours of studying the stars, we noticed a sphere moving slowly across the sky with a long tail behind it. [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] and I both marveled at the beauty of it. 'There is something divine about it.' [stargazing_host.GetFirstName] nodded slowly in response. 'It is. But it is hardly an omen of the end times as the peasants would have you believe. Unless it is the twin-tailed one, and then may Sigmar help us all.'
No it is not. But it is beautiful.

[stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] and I have been taking turns in making observations and recording everything. I cannot say that we have made any significant discoveries so far. We have made some progress, however, and learned a few things we did not know before.
The night is not over yet.

We have spent hours observing the stars and trying to look for anything out of the ordinary. Neither [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] nor I has made any noticeable progress so far. With most of the night gone already, it is unlikely that we will accomplish much more.
What a disappointing night.

We have spent hours observing the stars and trying to look for anything out of the ordinary. But neither of us has been able to make any significant progress. Which is disappointing, to say the least. But I can see that my host, [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName], is more disappointed than I am. [stargazing_host.GetSheHeCap] probably had very high hopes for the night.
So did I.

The sky was filled with ominously dark clouds already when we started our observations. As the hours drag on, it is only getting worse. You cannot see anything by now! Not a single star in sight! I suppose we might as well call it a night right here...
Curse this weather!

After spending the night together with [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName], I feel like we have become quite close. We seem to complement each other perfectly and the both of us are having a really good time!
I have gained a new friend!

Accepting the invitation to come here and spend the night studying with [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] was the correct decision. I have not had this much fun talking to someone in quite a while. We seem to understand each other perfectly!
Thank you my friend.

This night seems never to end. I am wondering why I even invited [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] in the first place. Nothing I have done so far seems to please [stargazing_guest.GetHerHim]. Whenever I try to start a conversation to lighten the mood, [stargazing_guest.GetSheHe] only answers with an obnoxious remark.
I cannot wait for you to leave...

I should just have thrown away [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s invitation the moment it arrived. This night has been nothing short of horrible. Listening to [stargazing_host.GetHerHim] hurling one insult after the other. One might wonder if that is the reason why [stargazing_host.GetSheHe] invited me here!
I have never been so offended!

Dawn is upon us as the first light appears on the horizon. I think we can agree that the night was an immense success. We took plenty of notes and learned a thing or two. Maybe we will have an opportunity to continue our combined research in the future?

An exhausting night finally ends. We worked throughout the entire night without any sort of noticeable progress at all. While it feels disappointing, I am confident that continued observations will yield superior results.

Time really does fly when you are having fun. We did not make any sort of noticeable progress in our attempted research. But the night was spent in good company, making it feel much less of a disappointment.
Let us do this again sometime.
Progress takes time.
Progress or not. I had a great time!
Time to go home.
Excellent!
That is disappointing.
What a shame.

Past midnight the second moon rose over the hills, and it was wrong. Morrslieb, the Chaos moon, swollen and green and far larger than any almanac said it should be, so bright that [stargazing_guest.GetTitledFirstName] and I cast two shadows. The longer I looked at it the more I was sure that something on its face was looking back.
Record everything. Every detail. Verena demands it.
Some things are not for mortal eyes. Look away.

Morrslieb rose tonight, huge and sickly green, while [stargazing_host.GetTitledFirstName] and I stood on the roof. [stargazing_host.GetSheHeCap] went white as chalk, and I do not think I was any better. The old almanacs speak of nights like this before every great war of the north.
I will not sleep tonight.

The Changer of the Ways hoards every secret ever written, and so must I. A true library of forbidden lore takes years and gold to gather, and every book in it will be a key to some door the gods have hidden. It is time my secrets had a home.
All knowledge is change!
Not yet. The threads are not ready.

Where shall the library stand? What I mean to keep there would send any priest of Sigmar screaming for the pyre, and sooner or later a Witch Hunter will come sniffing. I could hide it within the castle walls, or hide it in plain sight as an honest scholar's hall. Or I could raise it somewhere far away, where only the invited find the door.
Behind a false wall in [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName], where no zealot will look.
The library must fit into your castle. Your books will be hidden, but your household will sleep beside them.
In an honest scholar's hall. The best lie is in plain sight.
Nothing will stand in the way of a fine library, but anyone may walk in and wonder.
In a tower on an island, reached only by boat.
In a tower far out in the wilds.
Far from prying eyes the library can be as large as it needs to be, and a hunter will have to find it first.

The builder's plans keep changing on my table. I swear the ink moves when I look away. A hidden cabinet of a few dozen books would serve. So would a scriptorium where blind copyists write what the books tell them, or a labyrinth of shelves under a ceiling painted with eyes. And there is the plan he will not show me, the one that looks like the Crystal Labyrinth itself.
A hidden cabinet will do.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a small but useful library.
A scriptorium, with copyists who ask no questions.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a library where forbidden books can be copied as well as read.
A labyrinth of shelves, worthy of the Changer.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a great library with reading rooms, a scriptorium and sealed vaults.
A library to make the Impossible Fortress jealous.
[Root.GetFullName] will build a library worthy of the Architect of Fate, with every gallery, vault and secret door the plans can hold.

Forbidden books must be copied before they rot, or before the hunters burn them. Any desperate scribe in the town would do it for coin, though he may go mad and talk. There are others, cultists of the Changer whose hands were blessed with more fingers than they need, who copy a page in a heartbeat and never speak of what they read.
Hire the town scribes, and watch them.
Send for the blessed copyists.

Light is a danger to old paper and to secrets. Tallow candles are cheap, but the smell carries and the smoke stains. Lanterns of witch-glass burn with a cold blue flame that eats no paper and casts no shadow on the street.
Candles. We shall be careful.
Only the cold blue flame.

Some of these books will not stay closed. One hums at night, another weeps ink. Plain leather straps are cheap. Bindings sealed with sigils of warding cost a fortune, but they keep the pages shut, and keep whatever is in them inside.
Leather straps will hold.
Seal them with sigils.

And then the books themselves. I have a few already, stolen, bought or bargained from a dying man. A few is not a library. The black markets of Marienburg have lists, the ruins of Mordheim hold what the Witch Hunters missed, and some of the Changer's servants will trade a grimoire for a favour I may come to regret.
The books I have will be enough for now.
Buy, steal or bargain for every one!
[Root.GetFullName] will spare [Root.GetHerHis] purse, and the library will be the poorer for it.
[Root.GetFullName] will pay for the best, and the library will be the better for it.
It is a cupboard of secrets more than a library, and the catalogue fits on a single page that rewrites itself every new moon. But it is mine, and every book in it is a door.
The work is done. My library may not match the hidden vaults of the Magisters, but its shelves are full and its copyists silent. Somewhere among these pages is the next step on the path.

The library is finished, and it is a fine one. Scholars who should know better write to ask whether they may read in it, and I always say yes, for a while. The Changer will show me which of them to keep.
Time to open the books...
Let the reading begin!
The Library of Secrets
A Labyrinth of Lore

After months of work and a small fortune in gold, the library of [Root.GetFullName] holds the stolen learning of half the Old World. Its galleries turn in ways the builders cannot explain, its scriptorium copies what no honest temple would keep, and its vaults hold writings even the Colleges thought lost. It stands as a monument to the [Root.GetTitle]'s ambition.

No expense was spared. Under the eye of [Root.GetFullName] a labyrinth of knowledge has risen, and no two visitors agree on how many floors it has. Its shelves hold books written before Sigmar, its blue lamps never go out and its doors open only for those the library likes.\n\nSomewhere deep within, the Changer of the Ways is surely smiling.
Every page is a thread!
Now let me pull the threads.

The whole castle woke to screaming. One of the books caught fire on its own, and the flames that leapt from it were pink and blue and laughing. By the time the bucket chain came the shelves were ablaze, and the water only made the fire sing. We saved most of the books, but not everyone came out unchanged.
Better skin than books.
Ward the shelves properly this time...
[Root.GetFullName] will spend gold on wards and witch-glass, so the library suffers less.

A Witch Hunter has come to town, and he has been asking questions about the [Root.GetTitle]'s new library. This morning a crowd gathered at the gate, egged on by a priest of Sigmar, demanding to see what books I keep and who writes them.
Show them the honest shelves. Hide the others.
[Root.GetFullName] will change [Root.GetHerHis] plans to calm the townsfolk rather than to build the best library.
Let the hunter come. He will not leave.

Disaster! The crates of books I bought this spring have changed in the cellar. The words have crawled about the pages, a treatise on alchemy now reads as a book of nursery rhymes, and one volume has grown teeth. So much for leaving them there until the shelves were ready.
Save what can be saved.
Build a sealed store for them, at once!

Clan Skryre warlock-engineers have laboratories, yes-yes, and so must I! A true warp-laboratory takes time and much warptoken, but with one I will build weapons no rival has seen. The Council of Thirteen will tremble. Or at least listen.
For science, yes-yes!
Later. Spies are watching.

Where to dig the laboratory? Warpstone is precious and every rival in the Under-Empire wants mine. I could dig it deep under [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] where I sleep, though it may blow up under me. I could build it in the open warren, where the slaves can haul and fetch. Or far away, in a lost tunnel only I know.
Deep under my own burrow, where I can watch it.
The laboratory must fit under your burrow. It will be safe from thieves, but you will live beside it.
In the open warren. Slaves need to reach it.
Nothing will stand in the way of a fine laboratory, but any spy may creep in.
On an island, under the sea-caves.
In a lost tunnel far away.
Far from rival eyes the laboratory can be as large as it needs to be, and a thief will have to find it first.

The tunnel-master squeaks over his plans. A burrow with a bench and a crucible would serve. A workshop with forges and slave-wheels would serve better. A great warp-forge with lightning rods and tanks of glowing sludge would be better still. And there is the plan he hides, a laboratory to shame the halls of Skavenblight itself.
A bench and a crucible will do.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a small but useful laboratory.
A workshop with forges and slave-wheels.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a laboratory where devices can be built as well as tested.
A great warp-forge, worthy of Clan Skryre.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a great laboratory with forges, test-pits and warpstone vaults.
Something to make Skavenblight squeal with envy.
[Root.GetFullName] will build a laboratory to rival the halls of Clan Skryre, with every forge, vault and lightning rod the plans can hold.
A laboratory needs hands. Common clanrat slaves are cheap and many, though they lose fingers and die often. Skryre acolytes know which end of a warplock to hold, and they cost much warptoken.
Slaves will learn, or die.
Hire Skryre acolytes.

Warpstone burns and things explode. Every warlock-engineer remembers a laboratory that went up and took half a warren with it. Buckets of sand are cheap. Stone blast-walls and lead-lined vaults are not.
Sand buckets. We will be careful-careful.
Blast-walls and lead vaults!

The devices need parts: gears, pipes, coils and glass. Scrap from the surface is cheap and mostly rust. Dwarf-made parts, stolen from the holds, are true and strong, and stealing them costs many lives and much warptoken.
Scrap will hold. Mostly.
Steal dwarf-parts!

And then the warpstone itself, the heart of everything. I have a little already. A little is not enough. The Grey Seers hoard it, the traders of Clan Mors sell it dear, and there is a fresh-fallen shard on the surface that the man-things have not found yet.
The warpstone I have is enough for now.
Buy, steal, dig, all of it!
[Root.GetFullName] will spare [Root.GetHerHis] warptoken, and the laboratory will be the poorer for it.
[Root.GetFullName] will pay for the best, and the laboratory will be the better for it.
It is a damp burrow with a bench, a crucible and a smell that makes even skaven eyes water. But it is mine, and it has not exploded yet.
The work is done. My laboratory is no hall of Skryre, but its forges are hot, its slaves busy and its warpstone locked away. Soon-soon my rivals will see what I can build.
The laboratory is finished, and it is a fine one. Warlock-engineers from other clans have sent spies to see it, and some of the spies have even come back. Great weapons will be made here, yes-yes.
Time to build things...
Let the tinkering begin!
The Warp-Forge
A Wonder of the Under-Empire

After much digging and a heap of warptoken, the laboratory of [Root.GetFullName] is the talk of the Under-Empire. Its forges glow green day and night, its test-pits are scorched black and its vaults hold enough warpstone to blow a hole in the world. It stands as a monument to the [Root.GetTitle]'s cunning.

No warptoken was spared. Under the claw of [Root.GetFullName] a laboratory has risen that is squeaked of even in Skavenblight. Lightning crackles between its rods, warp-engines hum in its depths and its slave-wheels never stop turning.\n\nThe Lords of Decay have surely heard of it. That may not be good.
Build-build!
Now the world will fear me!

The whole warren woke to a great boom. A slave dropped a warpstone shard into the wrong vat, and the vat went up in green fire. By the time the bucket-slaves came half the workshop was ablaze. Most of the warpstone was saved, but many skaven were not.
Slaves are cheap. Warpstone is not.
Build blast-walls this time...
[Root.GetFullName] will spend warptoken on blast-walls and lead vaults, so the laboratory suffers less.

A Grey Seer has been squeaking to the clan that my laboratory is heresy against the Horned Rat, and that I mean to make weapons against the Council. This morning a pack of clanrats gathered at the burrow, demanding to know what I build and for whom.
Show them toys. Hide the true weapons.
[Root.GetFullName] will change [Root.GetHerHis] plans to calm the clan rather than to build the best laboratory.
Since when does a warlord answer to clanrats?

Disaster! The crates of warpstone I stored this spring are half gone. The slaves found them, licked them and some of them grew extra heads. The rest of the stone has gone soft and useless in the damp. So much for leaving it there until the vaults were ready.
Save what can be saved. Eat the slaves.
Dig a dry vault, at once!
Build a Library of Forbidden Lore
The Changer of the Ways hoards every secret ever written. Gather forbidden books into a library of your own, hidden from the Witch Hunters, and earn the favour of the Cult.
Dig a Warp-Laboratory
Every warlock-engineer worth his warptoken has a laboratory. Dig one of your own, fill it with warpstone and slaves, and build weapons to make the Council of Thirteen tremble.
Your capital has a Skaven laboratory.
You begin digging your warp-laboratory.
Warp-Burrow
A damp burrow with a bench, a crucible and a terrible smell.
Warp-Workshop
A workshop with forges and slave-wheels, where devices are built and tested.
Fine Warp-Workshop
A fine laboratory that spies of other clans try to see.
Warp-Forge
A great warp-forge glowing green day and night, the talk of the Under-Empire.
Wonder of the Under-Empire
A laboratory squeaked of even in Skavenblight, full of lightning rods and humming warp-engines.
There is a fourth road. Something keeps writing it in my margins.
Something offers to teach you all three mysteries at once.

For weeks now the margins of my books have filled with notes in a hand that is not mine, neat blue letters that fade by morning. Tonight they speak aloud. Why walk one slow road, the voice asks, when I can show you all three at once? The stars, the alembic, the will of the gods. A small favour later, nothing more. Everything has its price, and mine is so very small.
Teach me, then.
Begone! I will walk the road honestly.

The blue letters are back, and this time they do not fade. The debt is due, they write. The Changer of the Ways has need of a mind like yours, and a mind like yours has need of Him. Serve Him in secret, and you will learn more than the Order could teach in a hundred years. Refuse, and we shall see what you keep.
The Changer has my service.
I owe you nothing!
The gift may be taken back, with interest.
Or the voice may stay, and whisper.
